ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB=AD$, $AC=AE$, $BC=DE$, with point $E$ on $BC$. If $\angle EAC=\angle BAD$ and $\angle EAC=42^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle DEB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AC=AE$, and $\angle EAC=42^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle AEC=\angle C= \frac{1}{2} \times(180^\circ-42^\circ)=69^\circ$. \\
Since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle ADE$, \\
therefore $\angle AED=\angle C=69^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DEB=180^\circ-\angle AED-\angle C=180^\circ-69^\circ-69^\circ=\boxed{42^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB=AD$, $AC=AE$, $BC=DE$, with point $E$ on $BC$. If $\angle EAC=\angle BAD$ and $\angle EAC=42^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle DEB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AC=AE$, and $\angle EAC=42^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle AEC=\angle C= \frac{1}{2} \times(180^\circ-42^\circ)=69^\circ$. \\
Since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle ADE$, \\
therefore $\angle AED=\angle C=69^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DEB=180^\circ-\angle AED-\angle C=180^\circ-69^\circ-69^\circ=\boxed{42^\circ}$
